title: Crossfunc dependency mapping and safety matrix (WIP)
summary: Working draft: a compact and operationally actionable dependency map + safety matrix to coordinate cross-functional LLM canaries and A/B experiments. Focus: minimize blast radius, clarify ownership for signals and fallbacks, and provide lightweight runbook checklists that scale for Hosted / Dedicated / Private deployments.
content:
Purpose
This doc is a working artifact for coordinating canaries and A/B experiments which touch multiple teams (product, serving runtime, infra, SRE, security/compliance, support). It complements the rollout playbooks by making dependencies explicit and creating a single table of signals, owners, and automatic/manual fallback rules.

Scope and intent
- Scope: in-flight experiments that change model routing, fallback policies, prompt-level behavior, or introduce new model versions (including quantized variants and multi-variant routing).
- Not in scope: data schema migrations, non-LLM UI-only feature flags, billing-only experiments.
- Intent: provide a minimal ceremony (mapping + checklist) so teams can safely run progressive exposure without re-inventing communication patterns.

High-level roles and responsibilities
- Product rollout owner: drives hypothesis, acceptance criteria, sampling plan, and communication. (e.g., product PM)
- Experiment steward: day-to-day operator for the experiment (usually engineer on product or platform).
- Serving-runtime lead: verifies model compatibility, KV cache strategy, and batching config.
- Infra/SRE contact: validates capacity, synthetic traffic plan, and oncall escalation.
- Security/Compliance reviewer: approves data handling, PII leakage checks for private deployments.
- Support and CS rep: prepares templated responses and escalation contact.

Dependency mapping: what to check (compact matrix)
The minimal dependency mapping that must be completed before any progressive exposure begins. Fill this out as one-line entries in the experiment ticket.

1) Model & artifact dependencies
- Model binary version(s): list variants, size, quantization profile. (owner: serving-runtime)
- Prereq model conversions: new tokenizer, special op kernels, KV format changes. (owner: applied-ml)
- Inference config: batch sizing, latency SLO, top-k/top-p or temperature differences. (owner: serving-runtime)

2) Traffic & routing dependencies
- Routing path (percentage splits by cohort). (owner: product)
- Feature flags / route gates required. (owner: devex)
- Fallback model variants and mapping table. (owner: serving-runtime)

3) Capacity & infra dependencies
- Estimated peak qps and tokens/s under canary slices. (owner: infra)
- Autoscaler constraints and warm pools. (owner: infra)
- Synthetic traffic harness for signal amplification. (owner: sre)

4) Observability & telemetry dependencies
- Required signal set (see Signals section). (owner: observability)
- Dashboards and alert thresholds pre-created. (owner: observability)
- Logging/trace hooks for correlated session ids. (owner: serving-runtime)

5) Compliance & privacy dependencies
- PII/PIA review for dataset sampling if using customer prompts. (owner: security/compliance)
- Masking or retention rules enabled in private deployments. (owner: private-deployments)

Signals catalog and primary owners
This is the canonical short list of signals we rely on for canary decisioning. For each experiment the steward annotates which signals will be used as stop/continue criteria.
- Latency p50/p95/p99 (owner: observability)
- Error rate (5xx or internal inference error) (owner: serving-runtime)
- Quality delta (task-specific metric: e.g., rerank NDCG, summarization ROUGE proxy, hallucination rate) (owner: product / applied-ml)
- Cost per token / throughput efficiency (owner: infra / finance)
- Customer-facing regressions (support escalations, CS tickets) (owner: customer-success)
- Safety content score / policy triggers (owner: safety)

Safety matrix and gating rules (operational)
We use a simple three-band gating model: Green (go), Amber (investigate/hold), Red (abort/rollback). The steward assigns thresholds for each band prior to activation. The matrix below is a template:

Signal | Green | Amber | Red | Action owner
------ | ----- | ----- | --- | ------------
Latency p95 | <= 1.2x baseline | 1.2x-1.5x | > 1.5x | SRE/escalate to runtime
Error rate | <= baseline + 0.5% | +0.5% to +2% | > +2% absolute | Immediate rollback (automated)
Quality delta | >= -0.5% | -0.5% to -2% | < -2% | Product/Rollback or rollback to fallback model
Security triggers | no policy hits increase | small increase requiring review | sustained increase or high severity | Pause and security incident path
Cost per token | <= baseline * 1.3 | 1.3x-2x | >2x | Finance + infra review, throttle traffic
Customer tickets | <= baseline | small uptick | spike (>3x) | CS + PM triage

Operational notes on the matrix
- Wherever possible the Red path should be automated (immediate traffic revert to previous stable routing). Amber should create a paging action with documented mitigation steps. Green should still have monitoring for drift.
- Thresholds are contextual to experiment type; for small behavioral tweaks set tighter quality windows, for model size/quantization experiments allow larger cost efficiency windows.

Escalation and contact patterns
- Auto-fallback: routing controller to return traffic to pinned stable model within 30s of detecting Red threshold on latency or error rate. (owner: platform)
- Human paging: Amber band triggers oncall for experiment steward + runtime lead + SRE within 15 minutes.
- Full incident: Red band with user impact or safety signals escalates to incident commander and triggers the standard incident postmortem cadence.

Pre-canary checklist (must be completed)
- [ ] Dependency mapping completed in ticket (all 5 areas).
- [ ] Observability dashboards created and smoke-tested with synthetic.
- [ ] Autoscaler warm pools validated for canary slices.
- [ ] Fallback model pinned and smoke-tested.
- [ ] Communication: internal slack thread, oncall calendar event, CS template prepared.
- [ ] Compliance review completed if sampling customer prompts.
- [ ] Data retention settings verified for private deploys.

During-canary checklist (operational cadence)
- T+0: start at smallest cohort (e.g., 0.1% users) and run 20–30 minutes baseline observation.
- Continuous: monitor latency/error/quality windows and surface any Amber events to the steward.
- If Amber persists >30 min without clear mitigation, escalate to human triage.
- If Red occurs, automatic revert engaged and incident channel created.
- Maintain an observation log (short bullets) in the experiment ticket every 15 minutes for first hour, then every hour until stable.

Post-canary: acceptance and rollout steps
- Aggregate signals for the canary window (pre-specified length).
- Run targeted A/B significance tests for quality metrics.
- Validate cost delta and update cost forecast for full rollout.
- Perform security review on sampled outputs if enabled.
- Update model catalog metadata (version, commit, quantization notes).
- Schedule a short post-run debrief with SRE/runtime/product within 48 hours.

Lightweight recovery playbook snippets
- Latency spike with no errors: reduce batch size -> if unchanged, revert routing to prior model.
- Error spike localized to one region: divert region traffic to fallback region, create infra ticket, evaluate rollback.
- Quality degradation downstream (e.g., classifier false positives): pause rollout, lower exposure to 0, and reproduce on staging with same routing.

Special notes for Private deployments and Dedicated customers
- Include customer security contact in the dependency mapping. Private deployments may require manual approval for any rollback that touches their infra. Document the path explicitly in the canary ticket.
- For Dedicated capacity, ensure that reserved pool scaling does not silently block fallback capacity (i.e., fallback model must be available in the same pool or fallback will fail).

Open questions / TODOs (editorial list)
- Formalize which experiments can rely on automatic rollback vs. require human sign-off.
- Tie matrix thresholds to per-experiment risk score (low/med/high) so that higher-risk experiments get more conservative thresholds.
- Add small templated dashboards for common experiment classes (text-generation, rerank, embeddings).

Appendix: minimal ticket example (copy into experiment ticket)
- Hypothesis: new model v3 reduces cost by 20% with <=1% quality regression on summarization metric.
- Sampling plan: 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% over 4 waves, hold 2 hours/wave.
- Owners: product=Priya Rao, serving-runtime=Evan Holt, infra=Sofia Martinez, security=Maya Singh, CS=Diego Alvarez.
- Primary signals and thresholds: latency p95 (Green <=1.2x, Red >1.5x), quality delta (Green >= -0.5%, Red < -2%).
- Fallback: model v2.3 pinned as immediate revert target.
- Synthetic tests: run text suite X and traffic harness Y pre-activation.

Notes to steward (short)
- Keep the experiment ticket as the source of truth; update the one-line dependency map before activation.
- If unsure about threshold sizing, default to conservative (tight quality, looser cost).
- Use the one-click revert in the console for immediate rollback and follow up with incident notes.

Revision history
- 2024-11-02: initial draft (Priya Rao)
- 2024-12-12: added private deployment notes and recovery snippets (Evan Holt)
- 2025-02-15: added amber automation cadence and expanded signals list (Sofia Martinez)

End of working draft. Feedback welcome in the experiment ticket or #release-orchestra.
